summary:
Research product recording a new sourced core-path lead and one new high-consequence Surface on the accepted map (base version 3); preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

New sourced discrepancy found while reading the previously deferred transport surfaces: the appendEntries handler has two entry paths with different guards. Normal RPCs go through processRPC, which applies checkRPCHeader (enforcing the supported protocol-version window, raft.go:43-71) before dispatching AppendEntries (raft.go:1390-1413). The heartbeat fast path processHeartbeat calls appendEntries directly with no header check (raft.go:1415-1436), and net_transport classifies a pure AppendEntries (Term != 0, leader address present, no entries, PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm zero, LeaderCommitIndex zero) as a heartbeat (net_transport.go:660-686) and hands it to that handler at net_transport.go:724-733. On that route appendEntries can still step a receiver down, persist a newer term, adopt the sender as known leader and refresh lastContact — so the same request shape is version-gated on one path and not on the other.

Deliberately kept as a lead, not an obligation: the reachability premise (whether a peer outside the supported protocol window can in practice deliver a pure heartbeat) and the consequence are both unestablished, and no comment states the gate is intentionally skipped on the fast path. The product therefore adds one deferred high-consequence Surface with sources S40-S43 and feedback naming the premise investigation that must come next (read checkRPCHeader callers and the transport's version handling). No behavior, fact, requirement or previously accepted Surface was modified, so the confirmed in-scope ConfigurationStore violation and all existing results keep their original basis.

Run state: map accepted at version 3, first finding confirmed in scope (batching-FSM ConfigurationStore delivery), no pending review work.
